OnUse (protected override, EntropicBrew..rationale: Closed 2026-07-27 with guards G1 and G2. The loop shape was already right -- `while (Owner.HasOpenPotionSlots)` generate one potion and procure it, stopping when procurement fails (EntropicBrew.cs:21-28) vs `while player.has_open_potion_slot` at potions.py:1265-1271 -- and both halves that were wrong are fixed: the procure verb is now potions.py's try_to_procure (potions.py:1352-1375, PotionCmd.cs:28-53's ShouldProcurePotion + AfterPotionProcured), and the legacy generator is now the OUT-of-combat factory (potion_pools.py:135-147, PotionFactory.cs:31-34). See the guards for the executed witnesses.

guards.what: G1 (was LIVE -- CLOSED 2026-07-27): the brew procures through PlayerCombatState.add_potion instead of PotionCmd.TryToProcure, dropping both of that verb's hooks
guards.rationale: Closed 2026-07-27: the brew's in-combat arm procures through the ported verb. potions.py:1258-1271's loop calls `try_to_procure(ctx.hooks, player, potion)` (potions.py:1352-1375), which runs the `should_procure_potion` pass first and dispatches `after_potion_procured` on success -- PotionCmd.cs:28-53's two hooks, in that order. EXECUTED (2026-07-27): a combat holding Sozu (relics/sozu.py) and drinking an Entropic Brew ends with an EMPTY belt, which is the game's behaviour; the same combat without Sozu fills all three slots. WAS: potions.py called PlayerCombatState.add_potion, which ran neither hook, so Sozu was ignored and Belt Buckle kept 2 Dexterity it should have lost. The out-of-combat arm added alongside it goes through RunState.add_potion, which runs the same ShouldProcurePotion gate but not AfterPotionProcured -- harmless, because an executed `grep -rn 'override.*Task AfterPotionProcured' src/` returns exactly one implementer (Belt Buckle) whose body is guarded by `CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress` and is a no-op outside a fight.

guards.what: G2 (was LIVE -- CLOSED 2026-07-27): the LEGACY generator is the wrong factory -- it applies the in-combat exclusion the source deliberately avoids here, and rolls uniformly instead of by rarity
guards.rationale: Closed 2026-07-27: the legacy arm uses the OUT-of-combat factory the source asks for. potions.py:1258-1269 now forks only on which stream the roll runs against -- parity takes potion_pools.generate_random_potion (potion_pools.py:150-156), legacy takes potion_pools.legacy_random_potion_out_of_combat (potion_pools.py:135-147) -- and BOTH roll a rarity first and then pick inside that rarity's bucket over the WHOLE pool, with no CanBeGeneratedInCombat exclusion. That is PotionFactory.cs:31-34's CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat, which EntropicBrew.cs:23 calls on purpose even mid-combat, so Fairy in a Bottle, Fruit Juice and Regen Potion are reachable from the brew again. WAS: the legacy arm called potions.random_potion, which filtered exactly those three (the in-combat form, PotionFactory.cs:60-65) and picked uniformly over the id-sorted pool instead of rolling a rarity. EXECUTED (2026-07-27): a legacy combat brew fills all three slots off the full pool.

guards.what: G3: the PARITY generator is right -- rarity roll then NextItem, on Rng.CombatPotionGeneration, over the unfiltered pool
guards.rationale: Verified against the factory rather than the docstring. PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotion is one `rng.NextFloat()` bucketed at <= 0.1 Rare / <= 0.35 Uncommon / else Common, then `rng.NextItem(list.Where(Rarity == rarity))` (PotionFactory.cs:67-81). potion_pools.roll_potion_rarity (potion_pools.py:118-126) and generate_random_potion (potion_pools.py:129-135) are that pair exactly, over POTION_POOL, and the sim reads `rng_set.combat_potion_generation` (potions.py:1214) -- the same named stream the C# passes. Two draws per potion on both sides, which is what keeps the stream counter aligned; a wrong stream here would be grade A (compare audit/records/relic/lost_coffer.json G2).

guards.what: N1: `HasOpenPotionSlots` is evaluated AFTER RemoveBeforeUse, so the brew refills its own slot
guards.rationale: PotionModel.OnUseWrapper calls RemoveBeforeUse at PotionModel.cs:293, before OnUse at :327, so by the time the loop runs the brew's own slot is null and the loop fills it. The sim does the same: CombatState.use_potion nulls the slot (combat.py:605) before calling potion.use (combat.py:609), and `player.has_open_potion_slot` is `None in self.potions` (player.py:146-149) against the same fixed-length list. Both sides therefore end with a full belt from a full belt. Executed shape check rather than assumption: the loop terminates on both sides because each successful procure fills exactly one null slot (Player.AddPotionInternal's `_potionSlots.IndexOf(null)` and player.py:116-118).

guards.what: N2: the belt is 3 slots in the sim and grows to 5 in the game, so this potion's yield differs whenever the growth relics are held
guards.rationale: Closed 2026-07-27: the belt grows. RunState.add_potion_slots (run.py:632-638) is implemented and all three growth relics call it on pickup; RunState.max_potions is handed to every CombatState the run builds (run.py:1304-1322) and finish_combat copies the fixed-length belt back 1:1 (run.py:1328-1340). EXECUTED (2026-07-27): a fresh RunState reports max_potions 3, and after Potion Belt's after_obtained it reports 5 with five null slots. So one Entropic Brew now yields the same NUMBER of potions on both sides, and therefore the same number of CombatPotionGeneration draw pairs -- which is the compounding this entry was filed for. WAS: PlayerCombatState.MAX_POTIONS = 3 with no growth path. The mechanism's owners (audit/records/relic/potion_belt.json, audit/records/relic/alchemical_coffer.json) are matched per binding rule 3; potion_belt's own 'no-op stub' premise is likewise stale in today's code.
